sources.finding: Wails desktop app running Claude, Codex, Gemini, Aider, Amazon Q, OpenCode, custom commands or shells in tmux or psmux sessions that survive closing the app; attention inbox with one-click replies; desktop and ntfy notifications; project dashboard with git status and Claude and Codex usage; diff with hunk revert; tasks with due dates and dependencies; remote servers over SSH; export and import of sessions.

sources.title: Desktop CHANGELOG 1.1.27
sources.finding: 1.1.27 adds groundwork for phone access over Tailscale, which only reaches pairing in this release; earlier releases added per-session and per-tab git worktrees, including on servers.

sources.title: session/worktree.go
sources.finding: Optional per-session git worktree on its own branch in a sibling directory, so parallel agents edit different files.

sources.title: git_sync.go
sources.finding: Pushing and pulling from the branch badge, which counts unpushed and unpulled commits.

sources.title: ASMGR recovery-tasks
sources.locator: Task/TaskStatus fields; UpdateTask 544-650; RestoreTask; GetNextTask 917-977; project_tasks.go TransferTask; project_tasks_api.go; mcp/taskmaster.go
sources.finding: Desktop local tasks have IDs, tags, descriptions/details, status, priority, subtasks and dependencies. GetNextTask recommends unresolved work whose blockers are done; UpdateTask does not gate status by dependencies. Status can reopen done work. No archive or epic kind or dedicated acceptance-criteria/revision field. File backups preserve snapshots. Edits/undo retain IDs; cross-list moves can change a colliding ID and drop dependencies. Task Master is a client integration, not a product-owned agent task server.

sources.title: ASMGR recovery-notes
sources.locator: NotePage and ReadNotePages; project_tasks_api.go SetProjectNotePages; session/storage.go; session/backup_thinning.go; session_portable_api.go
sources.finding: Desktop project/session/tab notes are titled text pages, replaced through setters and persisted with session settings. No named author or freshness engine. Backups keep all last-hour versions, hourly through one day, daily through 14 days and weekly through 90 days, always newest, subject to ceiling. Session exports use JSON portable bundles, not remote runtime or a provider transcript export.

sources.title: ASMGR recovery-runtime
sources.locator: DialTimeout/CommandTimeout; token_usage_api.go constants and TokenUsageItem; interrupted_work.go; mobile/server.go route inventory; passwords/passwords.go
sources.finding: Desktop remote SSH connects in 10 seconds and bounds commands at 60 seconds. Token scans start after two minutes, repeat each 30 minutes and bound remote batches at two minutes; per-model/subagent counters include cache tokens. Mobile routes provide pairing/me/logout only. Session recovery/duplicate warnings do not provide exactly-once command replay. Password managers use backend-only values and 15-minute vault auto-lock; SSH host keys are checked.

sources.title: ASMGR recovery-git
sources.locator: gitPushAtPath 359-417 and gitPullAtPath; git_checkpoints.go private refs; git_checkpoint_cleanup.go; inspected git/diff/task API inventory
sources.finding: Push compares expected HEAD and destination before publishing; changed previews must be refreshed. Pull is fast-forward only. Private-ref checkpoint commits preserve file trees without changing HEAD/index and are restorable. These are local git controls, not PR merge/deployment authority or a test/spec gate. No task-owned artifact gallery or exact-commit review queue in the inspected API inventory.

sources.title: Agent Session Manager desktop: what leaves the machine, and pinned telemetry source inspection
sources.locator: README.md lines 374-377 (What leaves your machine); bounded search of the pinned Go backend and frontend/src for telemetry, analytics, PostHog, Segment, Sentry, Amplitude, Mixpanel, Bugsnag, Datadog, gtag and crash reporting, excluding go.sum, lockfiles and SVGs; outbound hosts in *.go reviewed
sources.finding: The README says nothing leaves the machine unless asked: the app talks to GitHub for its own updates, to an ntfy server if mobile push is configured, and to npx for Task Master; there is no telemetry. The source search found no analytics or crash client; outbound hosts are GitHub, ntfy, Google speech for opt-in dictation, and documentation links.
